title: Six socks are not six possible pairs
hook: Which method checks fewer pairs in this matching puzzle?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that six socks can be put together in 15 different pairs, so the checks grow fast with more socks, and distinct patterns cut this to one look per sock

misconception: Six loose socks need only a handful of checks to pair up.
objective: Without partner marks, every unordered pair is a candidate. Unique partner marks reduce the pictured task to one match per marked pair. The combinatorial growth explains the appeal of distinctive patterns.

recall.question: Eight socks with no marks: how many possible pairs could you check? With unique partner marks, how many matches are there to make?
recall.why: Without marks every unordered pair is a candidate: 8 × 7 ÷ 2 = 28. Unique marks leave one match per pair: 4. The candidate count grows much faster than the sock count.
